extracted.intended_audience: graduate students / advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry (Math 216 readers)
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook section collecting definitions, theorems, and concrete criteria for recognizing and using flatness of modules, sheaves, and morphisms (including local, infinitesimal, valuative, slicing, fibral criteria, and consequences such as openness, dimension behavior, and flat limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat = locally free for coherent sheaves (Corollary 24.4.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A coherent sheaf F on X is flat (over X) if and only if it is locally free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local freeness can be checked at stalks (see Exercise 13.7.F). This gives a geometric interpretation: for coherent sheaves on schemes, flatness is equivalent to being a vector bundle (locally free).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward of locally free under finite flat morphism (Exercise 24.4.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is a finite flat morphism of locally Noetherian schemes and F is a finite-rank locally free sheaf on X, then π_* F is a finite-rank locally free sheaf on Y. If Y is irreducible with generic point η, degree of π above η is n and F has rank r, then π_* F has rank nr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: transitivity of flatness (Exercise 24.2.H). Use base-change and rank computation at generic points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finitely presented flat modules are projective (Exercise 24.4.F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose A is a ring and M is a finitely presented A-module. Then M is flat if and only if it is projective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: show M is projective iff M_m is free for every maximal ideal m. The harder direction uses Hom_A_m(M_m,N_m)=Hom_A(M,N)_m (Exercise 1.6.G). Note: finitely generated flat modules that are not projective must not be finitely presented; an example (sketch) is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite flat morphisms have locally constant degree (Exercise 24.4.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finite flat morphisms have locally constant degree (i.e., the degree function on the base is locally constant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make precise as suggested (see 17.4.4 and Exercise 17.4.D(a)); Exercise 24.4.H and 24.4.G give tools to formalize locally-constant degree and its relation to π_* O_X being locally free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for flatness via π_* O_X for finite morphisms (Exercise 24.4.H)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is a finite morphism with Y reduced and locally Noetherian, then π is flat iff π_* O_X is locally free, which is equivalent to the rank of π_* O_X being locally constant (i.e., q ↦ dim_{κ(q)} (π_* O_X)_q is locally constant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial hint: Exercise 13.7.K. This gives a practical test for flatness of finite maps by checking the pushforward structure sheaf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for flatness over a regular curve (Exercise 24.4.K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π: X → Y is a morphism from a locally Noetherian scheme to a regular (locally Noetherian) curve. Then π is flat iff all associated points of X map to the generic point(s) of Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a geometric criterion (partial converse to Exercise 24.2.J). The statement can be generalized to coherent sheaves F on X by the same argument; check associated points of the sheaf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuative criterion for flatness (24.4.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism π: X → Y that is finitely presented, if π is flat then for every morphism from Spec of a discrete valuation ring (DVR) Y' → Y, the base change π' : X ×_Y Y' → Y' is flat and maps associated points appropriately. Conversely, if Y is reduced and locally Noetherian, this condition (checking on DVRs) is sufficient for π to be flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful way to visualize flatness via one-parameter tests. See Grothendieck EGA IV3.3.11.8 for proof and extensions without Noetherian hypotheses. Reducedness of Y is necessary (counterexamples referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat limits / closure are flat (24.4.12 and 24.4.L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given A a DVR and X an A-scheme locally Noetherian, if Y is a closed subscheme of the generic fiber X_η then the scheme-theoretic closure Y' of Y in X is flat over A; moreover this flat closure Y' is unique (only one closed subscheme of X restricting to Y on the generic fiber and flat over A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes 'taking flat limits' over one-parameter families; see Exercise 24.4.M for an explicit nonreduced example. You may weaken Noetherian hypotheses in many situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology behavior in flat families / semicontinuity
rubrics_metrics.description: In flat limits/coherent flat families, cohomology groups can only jump up (i.e., h^i can increase) in special fibers, while the Euler characteristic remains constant in flat families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated by explicit degenerations (twisted cubic degenerating to a nodal cubic with nonreduced point); formal statement given by the Semicontinuity Theorem 28.1.1 and constancy of Euler characteristic follows from flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful flatness characterizations (24.5.1 and 24.5.A/B)
rubrics_metrics.description: A B-module M is faithfully flat iff tensoring by M preserves exactness and reflects zero: for all complexes N'→N→N'' exact iff after ⊗_B M they are exact; equivalently M ⊗_B N = 0 implies N = 0; equivalently for all primes p (or all maximal ideals m) the fiber M ⊗_B κ(p) (or M/mM) is nonzero (Supp M = Spec B). Geometrically, a morphism π: X→Y is faithfully flat iff it is flat and surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these equivalent tests to check faithful flatness; faithful flatness is preserved by base change (surjectivity and flatness preserved).

rubrics_metrics.name: Going-Down Theorem for flat morphisms (Exercise 24.5.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flat morphisms satisfy the Going-Down property: for a flat ring map B → A, given primes q' ⊂ q in Spec B and a prime p' of A mapping to q', there exists a prime p of A mapping to q with p ⊂ p'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to considering the localized map and applying faithful flatness; see the exercise and visualize geometrically. There is a version paralleling the Going-Up theorem (Exercise 7.2.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat morphisms are open in reasonable situations (Exercise 24.5.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is locally of finite type and flat, with Y (and hence X) locally Noetherian, then π is an open map (i.e., sends open sets to open sets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline: reduce to affine case, apply Chevalley's theorem to get constructibility of π(X), then use Going-Down for flat morphisms to show closure under generization and conclude openness (Exercise 7.4.C). Hypotheses can be weakened to locally finitely presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimensions of fibers formula for flat morphisms (Proposition 24.5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a flat morphism π: X → Y of locally Noetherian schemes and points p ∈ X, q = π(p) ∈ Y, we have codim_X p = codim_Y q + codim_{π^{-1}(q)} p. Informally, (locally) dim fiber = dim X - dim Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare with Exercise 11.4.A: without flatness one only has an inequality. Use Going-Down to construct chains. Consequence: if X and Y are irreducible, fibers have pure dimension dim X − dim Y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: flat of relative dimension n (24.5.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π: X → Y (locally of finite type) is flat of relative dimension n if it is flat and all fibers have pure dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locally finite type hypothesis is to make behavior reasonable (preserved under base change). See Remark 24.5.7 on necessity of hypotheses and base-change subtleties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic flatness (24.5.N and Theorem 24.5.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is a finite type morphism to a Noetherian integral scheme and F is a coherent sheaf on X, then there exists a dense open U ⊂ Y over which F is flat. Improved version: if π is finite type, Y reduced, and F finite type, there is a dense open U such that π|_{π^{-1}(U)} is flat and of finite presentation and F is flat and of finite presentation over U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key tool: Grothendieck's Generic Freeness Lemma (7.4.4) and Stacks project references (tag 052B). Often used to reduce to a flat situation on a dense open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness is an open condition (Theorem 24.5.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y locally finite type of locally Noetherian schemes and F a finite type quasicoherent sheaf on X: (a) the locus in X where F is Y-flat is open; (b) if π is closed (e.g., proper), the locus in Y over which F is flat is open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part (a) reduces to a nontrivial commutative algebra statement (see Matsumura or EGA); Noetherian hypotheses can be weakened to local finite presentation (see EGA or Stacks tags).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local criterion for flatness via Tor vanishing (Theorems 24.6.1 and 24.6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local criterion: If (A,m) is a Noetherian local ring and M a finitely generated A-module, then M is flat iff Tor^A_1(M,A/m) = 0. More generally, for a local morphism (B,n)→(A,m) of Noetherian local rings with M a finitely generated A-module, M is B-flat iff Tor^B_1(M,B/n) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is powerful: flatness over the whole Spec A is determined by behavior at the closed point. Finite generation hypothesis is necessary (counterexamples noted). Proofs use Artin–Rees and Krull Intersection arguments; see exercises 24.6.A–24.6.C for reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinitesimal criterion for flatness (Exercise 24.6.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (B,n)→(A,m) is a local homomorphism of local rings and M a finitely generated A-module such that for every t≥0, M/(n^t M) is flat over B/n^t, then M is flat over B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines with previous vanishing lemmas to show flatness is determined by all infinitesimal thickenings; shows completions are flat over the ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slicing criterion for flatness (Theorem 24.6.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (B,n)→(A,m) be a local morphism of Noetherian local rings, M a finitely generated A-module, and t ∈ B a non-zerodivisor. Then M is B-flat iff t is not a zerodivisor on M and M/tM is flat over B/(t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful inductive check: reduce to checking for a divisor. Proof relies on Tor comparisons (Lemma 24.6.6) and local criterion for flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tor reduction lemma for slicing (Lemma 24.6.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If t ∈ B is not a zerodivisor on M (a B-module), then for any B/(t)-module N and all i, Tor^B_i(M,N) ≅ Tor^{B/(t)}_i(M/tM, N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by taking a free resolution of M and tensoring with B/(t); used in the proof of the slicing criterion and other Tor-vanishing arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slicing criterion in the source / relative effective Cartier divisors (Exercise 24.6.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose A is a B-algebra, A and B Noetherian, M a finitely generated A-module, and f ∈ A such that for all maximal ideals m of A, multiplication by f on M/mM is injective. If M is B-flat then M/fM is B-flat. Geometric corollary: a relative effective Cartier divisor in a flat family is flat over the base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the local criterion for flatness (Theorem 24.6.2) applied to localizations; this has an immediate geometric interpretation for flat families and relative Cartier divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fibral Flatness Theorem (24.6.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commuting diagram X --π→ Z and X --τ→ Y with ρ: Y→Z, and a finitely presented quasicoherent sheaf F on X and a point p ∈ X (q = π(p), r = τ(p)), under Noetherian or finite-presentation hypotheses the following are equivalent: (a) F is τ-flat at p and the restriction F|_r is π_r-flat at p; (b) ρ is flat at q and F is π-flat at p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem gives a criterion that relates flatness of the sheaf on the total space, flatness of the base-change morphism, and flatness on fibers; useful for checking flatness via base-change and vice versa (see EGA IV and Stacks tags).
